title: Existential–universal sentences: bounded models and decidability

based_on.title: Friendly Logics, Fall 2015, Lecture Notes 3
based_on.pages: 3–5 (§2, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3; constant-inclusive bound corrected)

summary: Choose all witnesses before the universal tests: a finite model bound turns satisfiability into a terminating search.
abstract: Some first-order sentences can be tested by looking through a finite list of small structures. The useful case here asks us to choose a fixed list of objects and then check a quantifier-free condition for every further choice. When the language has relations and constants but no other functions, a model can be shrunk to the chosen witnesses and constant values. This gives an explicit bound on its size and a finite search that decides whether any model exists. We explain how to enumerate the structures and check their truth tables, including equality and empty quantifier blocks. Finally, two examples show why functions and a different quantifier order can force every model to be infinite.
